ai.title: Default context-pruner params to empty object
ai.summary: Updates `.agents/factory/base.ts` to default `params` to `{}` when spawning `context-pruner` agents. Prevents potential `undefined` errors in downstream tool execution if `params` is not explicitly provided. Internal factory logic only; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: When the internal assistant system creates a specialized helper for trimming down conversation history, it now always provides an empty starting settings box even when none was given. This prevents the helper from crashing later when it tries to read those settings. Nothing you do as a user changes, this is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping inside the assistant-building toolkit.

ai.title: Include tree-sitter query files in @codebuff/sdk 0.1.11
ai.summary: Updated `@codebuff/sdk` to version `0.1.11`. Added `../packages/code-map/src/tree-sitter-queries` to the `files` array in `sdk/package.json`. Ensures tree-sitter query assets are bundled in the published SDK package.

eli5.text: If you build something using the Codebuff developer toolkit, the package now ships with extra reference files that the toolkit needs to read code structure. This fixes a problem where the toolkit could work on a developer's own machine but break when someone else installed it, because those files were missing from the published package. The developer toolkit package itself is what got updated today.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.12 adds build step to copy tree-sitter queries
ai.summary: The SDK build script now includes a `copy-scm-files` step to ensure `.scm` query files and `readme.md` from `../packages/code-map/src/tree-sitter-queries` are present in the `dist` output. This fixes missing asset errors by explicitly copying these non-TypeScript files alongside the compiled code. The change is scoped to `sdk/package.json`, bumping the version to 0.1.12.

eli5.text: Starting August 19, 2025, the software development kit used to build AI coding tools now automatically includes tree-sitter query files and a readme during its build process. Previously, these files were missing from the final output, causing errors. You wouldn't notice this as an end user, but developers building tools with this kit will see fewer setup issues. The change is already live in version 0.1.12.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.13 fixes code-map type import
ai.summary: Bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.13. Rename packages/code-map/src/types.d.ts to types.ts and update imports in index.ts and languages.ts to resolve SDK build breakage from importing .d.ts files.

eli5.text: The assistant's code-map component had a small import file named types.d.ts that was being loaded directly, which broke the build when the SDK tried to package it. The file was renamed to types.ts and two import lines were updated, and the SDK version was bumped to 0.1.13. This is a behind-the-scenes fix that makes the code-map load correctly; if you were watching the SDK build process, you would see it now compiles without the.d.ts-related error.

ai.title: Remove .ts extensions from code-map imports, bump SDK to 0.1.14
ai.summary: Removed `.ts` file extensions from relative imports in `packages/code-map/src/index.ts` and `packages/code-map/src/languages.ts` to align with standard module resolution. This change prevents potential build failures or resolution errors in environments that do not support explicit TypeScript extensions in import specifiers. The `@codebuff/sdk` package version was bumped to `0.1.14` to include these fixes.

eli5.text: The coding tools now load their helper files more reliably, which means fewer setup errors when projects are put together in some computing environments. You wouldn't see anything new yourself, but developers building things with these tools will hit fewer stumbling blocks during setup. This is already live, and developers using the kit will automatically get the smoother behavior once they update.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.15 adds custom tool definitions and README examples
ai.summary: Bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.15. Add customToolDefinitions parameter to CodebuffClient.run() for extending agent capabilities with Zod-validated tools. Update sdk/README.md with basic and advanced usage examples, including image handling and custom agent definitions.

eli5.text: If you use the Codebuff assistant inside your own software tools, you can now teach it new tricks. The assistant can accept custom tools you define, which are validated automatically, so your extended assistant behaves predictably. Updated written guides show how to connect, run simple tasks like creating a calculator, and handle advanced scenarios such as processing images. These capabilities are available now in the latest version.

ai.title: SDK v0.1.16 fixes getCustomToolDefinition typo and updates API
ai.summary: Renamed `getCustomToolDefinintion` to `getCustomToolDefinition` and exported corrected name from `sdk/src/index.ts`. `description` is now required in `CustomToolDefinition` type and function params; `endsAgentStep` default flipped to `true`. `sdk/README.md` updated to reflect new signature and import path. Breaking change for users relying on optional `description` or default `false` for `endsAgentStep`.

eli5.text: If you build tools that work with this coding assistant, the helper you use to describe your custom tools now has its old misspelled name corrected, and you must now always provide a short explanation of what your tool does when you set one up. The instructions for setting up these tools have also been rewritten in the guide. This is a breaking change, so any older setup that left that explanation out or relied on the old default behavior will need updating.

ai.title: Log full template object in run-programmatic-step
ai.summary: Expanded logging in `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts` to include the entire `template` object alongside its ID. Changed log key from `template` to `templateId` for the ID, and added `template` for the full object. Internal change affecting backend observability.

eli5.text: When an internal assistant process runs automatically, the system now saves a more complete note about what it was given to work with. Previously, the diagnostic logs only recorded the template's identifier; now they also capture the full template details alongside that identifier. This means anyone checking the backend logs can see the complete picture of what the process received, not just a label for it. The change is already active in the backend for anyone investigating why an automated step behaved a certain way.

ai.title: SDK: handle prompt-error server action
ai.summary: Added `onPromptError` handler to `WebSocketHandlerOptions` and subscribed to `prompt-error` events in `websocket-client.ts`. `CodebuffClient` now routes `prompt-error` actions to `handlePromptResponse`, rejecting pending promises with combined error messages using `buildArray` from `@codebuff/common/util/array`. This ensures SDK consumers receive proper error feedback instead of hanging on failed prompts.

eli5.text: You no longer get stuck when the assistant fails to respond to your prompt. Previously, if the assistant ran into an error while trying to answer you, the request would just hang forever. Now, when something goes wrong, you get a proper error message instead of waiting endlessly. This affects anyone using the SDK to build tools or applications that connect to the assistant.

ai.title: Fix context pruner message removal
ai.summary: Updated context pruner to remove exactly three messages (assistant tool call, input params, user instructions) instead of just the last assistant message. Removed expireMessages call for userPrompt in spawn-agent-inline handler. Prevents accidental deletion of user instructions prompt and leftover temporary messages.

eli5.text: When the system runs a cleanup to make room for new content, it no longer accidentally deletes the instructions you gave it. Previously, the cleanup only removed the last assistant message, which sometimes left behind extra temporary messages; now it removes exactly three messages (the assistant's tool call, its input parameters, and your original instructions) so your prompt stays intact. This affects internal agent sessions that hit the automatic context-trimming feature, and if you were watching the message history, you would see your user instructions surviving the trim instead of vanishing.

ai.title: strreplace allowMultiple flag blocks ambiguous edits
ai.summary: Added `allowMultiple` boolean to `str_replace` tool params, defaulting to false. `processStrReplace` now counts `old` string occurrences; >1 without the flag returns an error requesting a more specific string. Updated tool definitions in `backend/src/tools/definitions/tool/str-replace.ts` and `common/src/tools/params/tool/str-replace.ts` to reflect the new schema and remove XML tag closing instructions.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to replace a piece of text in a file, it now refuses if the old text shows up more than once unless you explicitly ask it to handle multiple matches. This stops the assistant from accidentally editing the wrong spot when your old text isn't unique enough. You'd notice it as an error message telling you to make your replacement text more specific if it matches several places in the file.

ai.title: Fix unparsable token in OpenRouter type definitions
ai.summary: Corrected unparsable token in OpenRouter type definitions. Replaced invalid character in `logitBias` documentation example with `<|end-of-text|>`. Affects `openrouter-chat-settings.ts` and `openrouter-completion-settings.ts` in `packages/internal`. Removes trailing semicolons in type definitions.

eli5.text: The assistant's configuration file had a stray, unreadable character in a comment meant to explain how to block certain text tokens from being generated. Developers cleaned up these type-definition files by removing invalid characters and trailing punctuation so the documentation reads correctly and the configuration parses without errors. You wouldn't notice anything as a user today, but if you looked at the files, the comments about logit bias settings now use valid placeholder text.

ai.title: Spawn agent params default to empty object
ai.summary: Updated `validateAgentInput` in `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts` to default `params` to an empty object `{}` before parsing. This fixes spawnable agent failures when no params are provided, ensuring schema validation handles undefined inputs gracefully. Scope limited to backend agent spawning utilities.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to spawn a helper agent without giving it any input parameters, the request no longer fails with a validation error. The system now treats a missing parameter set as an empty set instead of something broken, so agent spawning works in more cases than it did before. This only affects how the assistant launches helper agents behind the scenes.
